results.response_text:
Independent makers, academic researchers, and open-source diving technologists are actively building low-cost or DIY hardware and software pipelines for underwater cave and submerged passage mapping. Commercial systems (such as those by Stone Aerospace) cost tens of thousands of dollars, inspiring hobbyists and engineers to adapt consumer microcontrollers and sensors.
Notable DIY and Open-Source Mapping Projects
Camazotz-Ixchel: Developed as open-source firmware for a handheld underwater cave-mapping device running on RP2350 microcontrollers to generate live stick maps as divers navigate submerged tunnels.
ScubaBoard DIY SLAM/LiDAR Experimenters: Community technical divers and makers are designing custom instrument tubes attached to Diver Propulsion Vehicles (DPVs) housing 360-degree blue-light underwater LiDAR, depth sensors, and IMUs to capture precise cave cross-sections.
CavePI / University of Florida Robotics: Academic and open-source contributors have designed low-cost Autonomous Underwater Vehicles (AUVs) like CavePI aimed at autonomous navigation and mapping in GPS-denied, low-visibility underwater caves using edge-AI and semantic guidance .
DIY Arduino/ESP32 Sonar and Echo Sounders: Makers utilize platforms like Arduino and ESP32 combined with waterproof ultrasonic transceivers (such as JSN-SR04T) and depth transducers to prototype affordable underwater acoustic depth-profiling and mapping hardware.
If you're looking to build or use one of these systems, would you prefer details on acoustic/sonar approaches or optical/SLAM-based visual mapping?

Camazotz and Ixchel are two distinct deities within Mayan mythology and were not "built" as a single entity or structure.

Camazotz, whose name translates to "death bat" in the K'iche' language, is a fearsome bat spirit primarily associated with night, death, and sacrifice. He is mentioned in the Popol Vuh, the K'iche' Maya sacred book, where he is depicted as a bat-like being in the underworld of Xibalba. Camazotz is famously known for decapitating one of the Maya Hero Twins, Hunahpu, during their trials in the House of Bats.

Ixchel, on the other hand, is a significant grandmotherly creator goddess. She is revered as the patron deity of medicine, rain, and childbirth. Ixchel is also known as "Lady Rainbow" in many of her depictions in Maya art.

Brickspect is a fully automated vision defect detection system designed for manufacturers of building materials, such as paving blocks and hollow bricks. It utilizes vision cameras and machine learning algorithms to identify and remove defects in these materials. The system can detect damage on the upper surface of products, including cracks, discolorations, and other imperfections, as well as incorrect dimensions. Brickspect's algorithms for dimension analysis are based on laser triangulation, and it collects, reviews, and analyzes production process data to help avoid problems and costs in later stages of the manufacturing process.

Brickspect was made by Systems KSM Vision.

Brickspect is an AI-powered automated vision defect detection and quality control system designed for manufacturers of building materials like paving blocks and hollow bricks.
It was developed by KSM Vision, a deep-tech company based in Poland that specializes in optical quality control and production automation systems.
What Brickspect Does
The system integrates directly into manufacturing production lines to optimize quality control:
Defect Detection: It utilizes specialized vision cameras and machine learning algorithms to automatically spot damages on the upper surface of paving stones and blocks, such as cracks, discoloration, and structural flaws .
Height & Dimension Control: It relies on laser triangulation to accurately measure the precise dimensions of building blocks, filtering out items with incorrect heights or non-relicable anomalies.
